title: Prior winter SST gave no clear added next-winter forecast gain in three southern ocean boxes in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether prior winter sea surface temperature (SST) adds next-winter forecast skill in three fixed southern ocean boxes. We used NOAA ERSSTv5 and forecasts fitted to earlier years only. The reference model uses summer local SST, summer and prior winter Nino 3.4 SST, and time. Adding prior winter local SST reduced mean squared error by 10.81% in the South Atlantic box, 5.22% in the South Indian box, and 4.00% in the South Pacific box for 1981-2025. Conditional 95% five-year block intervals were -2.46 to 19.67%, -5.31 to 14.75%, and -3.36 to 11.90%. All three adjusted intervals also included zero. Rolling 30-year fits gave smaller gains and a small Pacific cost. Without tropical controls, the Pacific gain was larger and its interval excluded zero. Some late-period gains were also clearer. Thus the main full-period test gives uncertain added skill, with dependence on model controls and training history. This does not show that ocean heat storage is absent. One revised surface product, 45 score years, fixed boxes, linear fits and uncertainty conditional on the forecast history limit the result. Code, monthly aggregate evidence, all forecasts, source hashes, figures and numerical checks are included.
